fullDaySay: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
💧 A woman, maybe 60s, with a wiry build returns with water: +4 clean.
💧 A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic returns with water: +3 clean.
A person, maybe 60s is stitching a tear shut by the door light, squinting at every stitch.

"Hey." A man, maybe 40s, with a long braid settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 40s, with a long braid.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Rain. Steady, cold, honest rain.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
Someone told a joke by the fire. You hear A man, maybe 40s, with a missing fingertip laugh — a real one.
A person, maybe 40s, with restless hands is hurt — a fall, a thorn, a bad step. (health 78/100)
A person, maybe 60s traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
You remember the Crowbar at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Rain poncho at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
A person, maybe 40s, with a gap-toothed grin will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
📋 A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm mutters something under their breath. You catch only the last word: "again."
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Ruth," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Ruth." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Ruth).
...and then it lands: A woman, maybe 20s, with a shaved head speaks 🇳🇴 Norwegian. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Mia.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Mia).
Mia speaks only 🇳🇴 Norwegian. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.
(They mime walking — pointing at themselves, then at you, then toward the trap line. The meaning is unmistakable: come with me.)
"Seymour," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Seymour." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Seymour).
You eat Dried meat and Trail mix (1400 kcal).
You take 4 logs from the woodpile for the road home. (12 left for the hearth.)

"Abigail," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Abigail." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Abigail).
...and then it lands: A person, maybe 60s speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
"Sukhman," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Sukhman." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Sukhman).

Travel 1 tile to grove.
— Nut trees —
Mast crunches underfoot — last season's nuts, sprouting or rotting. The trees don't waste anything.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
You see smoke on the horizon. Thornfield — 10 people, 3 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 3 plants — 3 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Unfamiliar unknown shoots — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Unfamiliar unknown shoots — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND **Green Thumb, Literally**. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.

A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 5× unknown nuts, 4× unknown shoots, 3× unknown shoots. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
2 unprocessed hauls onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 3 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.
Seymour picks through the bag, frowning. Nothing they can name with confidence. (8 ticks)
Seymour picks through the bag, frowning. Nothing they can name with confidence. (8 ticks)

You break ground behind the hall — bed 4 of 4, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
The stash count is off. 1 stone missing. Nobody saw anything. Everybody suspects something.
You catch fragments by the fire — A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic telling Sukhman about you. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.
📖 LEARNED: Gossip Network (Level 1). You hear things. People tell you things. You remember who told you what.
You catch fragments by the fire — Seymour telling A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm about you. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.
You catch fragments by the fire — Mia telling A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic about A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm. The story's getting bigger than what happened.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1020 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 40s, with a missing fingertip is showing A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair how to tie a snare. Hands patient. It takes three tries.

A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic spends the afternoon with the vine with thick-skinned round fruit — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
From the lumped bag: Muscadine Grapes — named, and out.
★ IDENTIFIED: Muscadine Grapes. Muscadine. Thick-skinned wild grapes. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 The vine with thick-skinned round fruit — THAT's what A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic was describing. Muscadine Grapes. It clicks like a key turning.
Seymour was watching. Now they know Muscadine Grapes too.
A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair came back with 859 kcal of something edible. The pantry can't take it all — 430 kcal in, 429 kcal eaten at the fire.
Mia traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
Raniera and Seymour lingered over the fire together.
Jesse and Ruth lingered over the fire together.
🍽️ Rosa looks at the full shelves and waves off the day's share. "No more into the store — we eat at the fire, and the shelves keep."
A runner from Stonebridge, dusty and direct: "Your foragers are stripping our side of the southeast ground. Back off — or we'll talk with teeth." (Trust -3. The commons cuts both ways.)

Fresh-cut stems on the northeast ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Thornfield's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)
A runner from Ashford, dusty and direct: "Your foragers are stripping our side of the northwest ground. Back off — or we'll talk with teeth." (Trust -3. The commons cuts both ways.)
You've started noticing: A man, maybe 40s, with a long braid and Ruth never speak. It's not new. (Something old lives in Haven.)
You've started noticing: A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair and A man, maybe 40s, with a missing fingertip never speak. It's not new. (Something old lives in Haven.)
— DAY 4 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Muscadine Grapes — named and noted.

👀 the woman in her 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm talks about wanting to belong somewhere the way people talk about weather — often, and with no plans to change it. The real wanting is somewhere they keep not looking.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm).

📋 A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm folds their arms. "Sure. Your call. For now."
A woman, maybe 20s, with a burn-scarred forearm steps closer. "We need to talk. About who's actually running things here."
"Zoe," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Zoe." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Zoe).
"Jesse," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Jesse." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Jesse).
"Rosa," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Rosa." You'll remember that.

You are full enough.
The pantry is in the hall. Your hands are not.

You catch fragments by the fire — Seymour telling A man, maybe 40s, with a missing fingertip about you. Three retellings in, nobody remembers what actually happened — but everyone has opinions.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to creek.
— Moving water —
The water is cold enough to hurt your teeth. Downstream the creek bends out of sight, and you want to follow it. That's the problem with creeks.
It followed you. The drumbeat with no drummer is here.
Something big pads at the edge of the clearing — then thinks better of it. This ground is already claimed.
✅ You saw the creek. Jesse nods. "Good. Now we know." (+integration)
